messages:
raj: Quick question — we're seeing a short spike of 502/504s from prod-ingress over the last 30m. Where's the best place to pull graphs + traces for a quick postmortem? :thinking:

emily: Start with Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ingress/ingress-errors (panel: upstream_502, upstream_504, proxy_5xx). Look at the timeseries stacked by upstream (svc) and by node. Also open the request-id trace view in Tempo.

jess: If you have a sample request-id from the nginx access logs you can get a trace in Tempo: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOTOKEN" "https://tempo.redwood.internal/trace?trace_id=<TRACE_ID>" — or just click the "open in tempo" link from the log line in Kibana.

raj: thanks. where are the ingress logs? I remember there are 2 places (proxy + origin) — which query to run so I get origin vs proxy 502?

emily: In Kibana: index ingress-logs-* and use this quick filter: 
```
http.status_code: (502 OR 504) AND kubernetes.pod_name:~"ingress.*"
| group by: upstream_name, kubernetes.node_name
| show: message, x_request_id, upstream_status
```
That separates proxy vs upstream (upstream_status shows origin code).

jess: Also check Loki for nginx errors if Kibana is slow: 
```
{app="nginx-ingress"} |~ "(502|504)" | json | unwrap upstream_status
```
Works for recent windows (last 1h).

alerts-bot: [ALERT] prod-ingress-high-5xx fired (peak 00:27 UTC) — group: ingress, severity: P2. https://alerts.redwood.internal/alerts/2345 :rotating_light:

sam: Quick triage checklist: 1) confirm whether upstream_status is 5xx (origin) or 502 from proxy; 2) check pod restarts / OOM in kube events; 3) check node CPU/IO for connection drops; 4) check rate-limiter / WAF hits.

raj: grabbed a few request-ids from Kibana. For one trace the upstream_status is 502 (origin) and the origin pod shows a connection reset in the logs. Any good dashboards for pod-level resource spikes?

emily: Use the kube-pod-resources dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/kube/pod-resources — filter by namespace=prod and pod name from the trace. Look at cpu/memory and socket backlog. Also check horizontalpodautoscaler events: 
```
kubectl get hpa -n prod
kubectl describe hpa <name>
```

jess: If autoscaler failed to scale, check the KEDA/controller logs and metric server metrics. KEDA used to throttle scale-up if metrics come in bursts.

sam: For alert tuning: the prod-ingress-high-5xx alert currently fires at >1% 5xx for 5m. If this is noisy during short bursty failover windows we can: raise to 2% for prod OR add a suppression window for <10m bursts. Happy to file a PR to rules if you think it's a false positive.

raj: For now I'm attaching two traces + the grafana panels to the incident doc. Root cause looks like origin pod overload + restart loop during a deploy spike. Can someone temp-mute the alert for 20m while we investigate? @eng-sre

emily: @eng-sre can you mute prod-ingress-high-5xx for 20m? I think manual scale to 5 replicas and rollout pause helped.

alerts-bot: Mute request received: prod-ingress-high-5xx — pending approval from eng-sre oncall.

sam: Approved and muted for 20m. :white_check_mark: I also bumped HPA min replicas to 3 and added a note to follow up with infra on a better scale policy.

raj: great, thanks everyone. I'll add the kibana queries + tempo links to the incident doc and include the pod logs. Follow-up: open a small ticket to evaluate alert thresholds and add origin_vs_proxy breakdown to the alert to reduce noise.

emily: Sounds good. Ping me on the ticket for the HPA policy changes. :+1:

jess: Adding one more tip for next time: if you need sample curl for reproducing with request-id header: 
```
curl -v -H "x-request-id: test-$(date +%s)" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_TOKEN" \ 
  "https://prod.api.redwood.com/v1/generate" --resolve api.redwood.com:443:<ingress-ip>
```
Use --resolve to hit specific ingress node.

raj: saved. last message: incident doc updated, attaching trace IDs and grafana snapshots. closing the immediate triage. Thanks. :slightly_smiling_face:
